newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico may place $1 bln more in debt in 97 -Werner.
newsitem.headline: Mexico may place $1 bln more in debt in 97 -Werner.

text.p: Mexico may place Eurobonds worth up to $1.0 billion in the remainder of this year to boost its presence in Europe, Martin Werner, deputy finance minister, said in an interview on Tuesday.
Mexico has virtually met its refinancing needs for the year, so the government will use the rest of this year to secure some of its borrowing needs for 1998.
One path will be to place more debt in diverse European markets, such as Spain, Portugal, France or Switzerland, Werner told Reuters.
"In the second half of the year... the federal government's borrowing needs are practically nil, however, we think we would like to continue with our policy of diversifying our markets," Werner said.

"Since we have had very little activity in Europe, we want to consolidate our presence in certain currencies so that when there is a single currency in Europe, Mexico will be a issuer known in all those markets...," he said.
He noted that the placements would likely be on the smaller side of what the federal government is used to issuing, likely between $100 million and $300 million.
"I think that if there are good conditions (the total) could be around $1.0 billion," Werner said.
Mexico has been active recently in placing bonds denominated in Italian lira, German marks and British pounds, as well as yen and U.S. dollars.
Plans for a single currency in the European Union means Mexico is now looking at becoming better known there.

"So we are looking at Spain, Swiss francs, Portugese escudos. We are looking at the European markets to see if things will be possible there," he said, adding that France could be one of those markets.

But he said that the debt placements would be at a slower rhythm than at the start of the year, when the government placed a number of issues to cover maturing debt and for other uses such as paying back a floating-rate note that it called.
"The situation... will be oriented towards refinancing some debt for coming years, to start refinancing debt for 1998, which is a year with a small amount of maturing market debt," he said.
